sections.name: OpenAIProvider
sections.title: OpenAI provider class
sections.what: Implements the common provider contract for OpenAI. It reports whether OpenAI is configured and, when asked to chat, removes the provider prefix, sends the request and returns a standard reply.
sections.why: Lets the router use OpenAI without knowing its details.
sections.watch_out: The router matches providers by the name 'openai', so renaming this provider breaks routing for OpenAI models.

summary: Adapter that lets the model router call OpenAI through the project's existing OpenAI helper.
purpose: Makes OpenAI one of the choices the router can use.
why: Likely reason: the router needs one common way to call every provider. The helper itself lives in another file.
how: 1. Reports whether OpenAI is configured. 2. Removes an openai/ prefix from the model name if present. 3. Asks for a JSON reply when requested. 4. Calls the shared OpenAI helper with retries turned off. 5. Returns the text, model name, provider name and token counts.
inputs: A model name, the chat messages and optional call settings.
outputs: A standard model reply with text, model name, provider name and usage counts.
risks: Retries are off, so a short OpenAI outage fails at once. The router's fallback is the only second attempt, and in the current settings it uses the same model, so there is no real retry.
debug: If OpenAI calls fail, look for the router's log line naming the provider and the error. Confirm the configured check returns true. Check that the model name has no stray prefix.
